name: Ice Finder
plain_text: Finds frozen water hidden in soil or under the surface.
importance: Water ice means drinking water, rocket fuel and oxygen for future bases.

name: Ozone Mapper
plain_text: Maps the ozone layer by measuring how much ultraviolet light the air absorbs.
importance: Ozone shields life from UV, so it shows how safe a world's surface is.

name: Air Sniffer
plain_text: Measures which gases are in an atmosphere and how they change with height.
importance: Air makeup decides if a world can be breathed, and how it loses gas to space.

name: Chemistry Lab
plain_text: Analyzes rock, soil or gas samples to find which elements and minerals are in them.
importance: Chemistry tells us if a place ever had water and if it could host life.

name: Radiation Meter
plain_text: Counts harmful particles from the Sun and deep space.
importance: Astronauts and electronics need to know how much radiation they will face.

name: Oxygen Maker
plain_text: Turns carbon dioxide from the air into breathable oxygen.
importance: Making oxygen on site means crews do not have to carry all of it from Earth.

name: Camera
plain_text: Takes pictures in visible light of the ground, sky or the spacecraft itself.
importance: Pictures pick landing sites, spot hazards and show the public what we found.

name: Heat Mapper
plain_text: Measures surface temperature using infrared light.
importance: Temperature shows where ice can survive and where a base could stay safe.

name: Shadow Imager
plain_text: Sees into permanently dark craters using faint starlight or ultraviolet light.
importance: Ice hides in places the Sun never reaches, so we need a way to look inside.

name: Terrain Mapper
plain_text: Measures heights to build 3D maps of hills, craters and valleys.
importance: Maps make safe landing and driving routes.

name: Rock Grinder
plain_text: Grinds or digs into a rock so instruments can study fresh material.
importance: Weathered surfaces hide the real chemistry, so you must get below them.

name: Interior Probe Kit
plain_text: Listens for quakes and measures heat flow to learn what a planet is like inside.
importance: The inside tells us how a planet formed and whether it is still active.
